obligations.finding: android/app/src/debug/AndroidManifest.xml sets android:usesCleartextTraffic="true" on <application>, i.e. for every host. Its comment and the only consumer (VanGatewayClient.defaultGatewayBaseUrl, which returns http://127.0.0.1:8787 only when BuildConfig.DEBUG and no VAN_GATEWAY_BASE_URL) need loopback only. The main manifest sets no networkSecurityConfig, so with targetSdk 36 release is cleartext-off by platform default, not by an explicit declaration. The same debug manifest exports RiveCandidateHostActivity with no permission.
obligations.proves: Cleartext is admitted only to loopback in debug and nowhere in release, and that holds in the merged manifests actually packaged.
obligations.preconditions: Built debug and release variants of com.dial.van from the admitted source; aapt2/apkanalyzer available.
obligations.stimulus: Inspect merged manifests and the packaged network-security config; on a debug build, attempt HTTP to 127.0.0.1 and to a non-loopback test host.
obligations.observable: Debug: loopback HTTP succeeds; non-loopback HTTP fails with CLEARTEXT_NOT_PERMITTED. Release: merged manifest has no usesCleartextTraffic=true; base-config cleartextTrafficPermitted=false (explicit); no exported debug-only activity.
obligations.negative: A non-loopback cleartext request in debug succeeding fails the obligation; any exported activity present only for development in release fails it.
obligations.recovery: Not applicable (static configuration); regression guard is the merged-manifest check in CI.
obligations.environment: JVM/host for manifest inspection; emulator for the debug request check. Not handset acceptance.
obligations.pass_evidence: Merged-manifest dump for both variants, the network-security XML, and the two request outcomes, bound to the APK SHA-256.
obligations.proposed_change_for_owner: Replace app-wide usesCleartextTraffic in the debug overlay with a debug network_security_config permitting cleartext only for 127.0.0.1/localhost; declare an explicit release config with cleartext off; restrict or drop export of RiveCandidateHostActivity. Application change under android/: needs unit admission and a ledger authorization.

current_review.fix: Explicit cleartext-off main policy; debug exceptions restricted to exact localhost/127.0.0.1/::1; exported debug rig requires android.permission.DUMP. Existing owner continuation authorization covers this confirmed baseline maintenance; no new frontend design or unit acceptance is asserted.
current_review.tests: 3 host checks, 195 app units, debug and instrumentation assembly and lint pass. New Android framework/real HTTP and rig-permission tests await hosted execution.
current_review.release_limit: Actual release manifest processing refuses without VAN_DEPLOYMENT_PROFILE_FILE; no fake profile or signer was supplied.
current_review.runtime_evidence: Run 39723196572, NetworkSecurityRuntimeTest: both tests pass (actual loopback HTTP, blocked non-loopback HTTP, exact framework policy, privileged debug rig). Instrumentation overall failed a separate legacy deep-link timing assertion; full release/handset and unit acceptance remain pending.

obligations.finding: IdempotencyService.begin (backend/van_gateway/idempotency/service.py:96-113) lets a same-hash IN_FLIGHT claim be retaken after STALE_CLAIM_SECONDS (900 s) and the caller re-executes, relying on CommandMissionLink.open -> existing_for_command (command/mission_link.py:107-133) to return the existing mission. That is check-then-act. The database does carry a guard: storage/db.py:162 creates UNIQUE INDEX idx_missions_source_command on json_extract(authority_envelope_json,'$.source_command_id') (confirmed in the schema snapshot, read with immutable=1). No code path catches the resulting IntegrityError, and no test exercises stale retake or concurrent open for the same command_id.
obligations.proves: A retaken or concurrent execution of one command yields exactly one mission and one downstream effect, and the losing path returns that mission rather than an error or a second effect.
obligations.preconditions: Isolated store in tmp_path; a command whose execution opens a mission.
obligations.stimulus: (a) claim, age updated_at_unix past 900 s, re-begin with the same hash, re-execute; (b) two concurrent opens for the same command_id racing past existing_for_command; (c) crash after mission insert but before idempotency complete, then retry.
obligations.observable: One missions row for the source_command_id; claim_count incremented once per retake; every caller receives the same mission_id; no unhandled IntegrityError.
obligations.negative: A different-hash attempt under the same key still raises IdempotencyConflict and leaves the original row unchanged (existing test_a_conflicting_attempt_does_not_poison_the_original_claim). A retake before 900 s is refused.
obligations.recovery: Case (c) resumes onto the existing mission without duplicating its effect.
obligations.environment: Backend source test (pytest), SQLite; Postgres too if the store is admitted for it (T-VAN-CX-008-POS).
obligations.pass_evidence: Test ids and output on the frozen baseline SHA, plus a mutation showing that removing the unique index or the existing_for_command check makes a case fail.

current_review.correction: test_recovery_matrix.py already covers stale claim retake returning the existing mission; the earlier finding overstated that test absence.
current_review.reproduced_defect: Two separate Store/CommandMissionLink instances both read no mission; one then raises idx_missions_source_command IntegrityError.
current_review.fix: On an integrity error, return the committed winning mission only if one exists for this command; otherwise propagate the original error. Preserve the unique index.
current_review.tests: 53 focused recovery/contract tests and 46 command API integration tests pass. Forced two-writer race returns one mission and one created event; unrelated primary-key failure still raises.
current_review.remaining: Whole-orchestrator downstream-effect deduplication, crash/recovery and admitted-store variants remain BE-003 acceptance work.
current_review.post_insert_guard: A further negative control showed a broad integrity handler could swallow a failed post-insert learning write. Recovery now requires the exact source-command uniqueness constraint; 100 related backend tests pass, including the real post-insert NOT NULL failure. Evidence: receipts/MISSION_POST_INSERT_BEFORE.txt and MISSION_RACE_VALIDATION.json.

obligations.owner_unit_correction: PRE-001 recorded OBS-003 under BE-028 (Automation, reminders and schedules). The browser approval flow belongs to BE-025 (Browser, remote interaction, artifact and share intake). Corrected here and in DISPOSITIONS.json.
obligations.finding: Removal in 652ef3f3 of test_owner_approval_resumes_same_browser_task left only refusal tests (cannot widen domain, cannot exceed class, advisory answer cannot resume). BrowserAPI.consume_resume_authorization (backend/van_gateway/browser/api.py:808) implements the positive path: single-use ACTIVE browser_scope_authorizations row, domains and class checked, conditional UPDATE to CONSUMED. Transition tests (test_browser_review_i3) cover WAITING_FOR_OWNER -> RESUME_AUTHORIZED but not an end-to-end continuation of the same task.
obligations.proves: A genuine, exact owner approval continues the same task_id within the approved scope exactly once.
obligations.preconditions: A browser task in WAITING_FOR_OWNER with a pending scope request; an enrolled owner device.
obligations.stimulus: Owner issues the exact approval through the production route; worker requests /assignments for that task within approved domains and class; then a second resume attempt.
obligations.observable: Same task_id moves RESUME_AUTHORIZED -> RUNNING; authorization row CONSUMED with consumed_at_ms; the continued step executes inside the approved domains; second attempt gets 409 BROWSER_RESUME_AUTHORIZATION_MISSING.
obligations.negative: Existing refusal tests stay green; concurrent double resume spends the authorization once.
obligations.recovery: Restart between approval and assignment keeps the authorization ACTIVE and resumable once; expiry yields refusal, not continuation.
obligations.environment: Backend source test with the real BrowserAPI and store; provider browser stubbed only below the assignment boundary.
obligations.pass_evidence: Test output on the frozen baseline SHA with readback of the task and authorization rows.

current_review.finding: The legacy consumer alone is not a positive production path: _sync_waiting_owner_decision keeps advisory APPROVED/ANSWERED tasks WAITING_FOR_OWNER and requires a fresh sealed command. No production INSERT into browser_scope_authorizations was found; the one insert is in test_browser_review_i6_scope.py. The existing signed browser-plan path has its own source E2E tests, but that does not prove this same-task boundary-resume contract.
current_review.disposition: Keep OPEN; bind a genuine supported sealed-command continuation and prove the same-task contract in BE-025. Do not manufacture legacy ACTIVE rows or turn an advisory decision into authority.

obligations.finding: Root cause reproduced with a sqlite3.connect/os.mkdir audit hook: backend/van_gateway/app.py:3856 executes app = create_app() at import, and Settings.database_path defaults to the relative 'data/van_gateway.sqlite3' (config.py:51). Importing van_gateway.app with cwd at the repo root makes Store.__init__ (storage/db.py:2551) create data/ and DocumentService (documents/service.py:32) create data/documents (mode 0700) next to the tracked schema snapshot. Observed trigger: tests/contracts/test_artemis_console_boundary.py::test_console_session_is_hardware_device_proofed_and_proxy_is_hermes_governed (imports the module-level app). The tracked file stayed byte-identical (sha256 2599f07d...f95e). The WAL/shm side files seen earlier are not explained by this; see probe_result.
obligations.proves: No test, tool or import writes beside or into the tracked data/van_gateway.sqlite3, and runtime never uses a cwd-relative database path.
obligations.preconditions: Clean checkout; tracked snapshot hash recorded.
obligations.stimulus: Run every canonical suite root from the repo root and from backend/ with an audit hook on sqlite3.connect and os.mkdir; import van_gateway.app with no VAN_DATABASE_PATH.
obligations.observable: Zero opens of the tracked path and zero new entries under data/; snapshot hash unchanged; importing the module does not create directories.
obligations.negative: Starting the gateway without an explicit absolute VAN_DATABASE_PATH in a non-test deployment refuses rather than writing a relative path.
obligations.recovery: Not applicable; regression guard is the audit-hook check.
obligations.pass_evidence: Audit-hook log (empty) and before/after snapshot hash on the frozen baseline SHA. Also an owner decision on whether the snapshot remains a tracked fixture.
obligations.proposed_change_for_owner: Make the app factory lazy (no create_app() at import) or have tests use a tmp database; give Settings no relative default in production. Application change: needs unit admission and a ledger authorization.
obligations.probe_result: Audit hook (sqlite3.connect + os.mkdir) over trading/tests/test_oci_trading_topology_bootstrap.py + tests/hermes/test_profile_layout.py: 48 passed, no events. Over all of tests/contracts: 1,525 passed, 4 skipped, exactly two events (mkdir data, mkdir data/documents, both from test_artemis_console_boundary importing the module-level app) and zero sqlite3.connect to the tracked path. Snapshot sha256 unchanged (2599f07d79e698115dddf647deef263efb927d8de6c8bafc7a08e935fa29f95e). The WAL/shm side files observed earlier are therefore NOT explained by tests/contracts or the two suites above; their source remains unidentified (candidates not yet probed: backend suite run with cwd at the repo root, tools/ops/backup.py defaults). The obligation's audit-hook stimulus over every canonical root is what closes it.
